title: Place Value and Ordering: Decimals and Negative Numbers
seo_title: Year 7 Place Value Worksheets: Decimals, Negative Numbers, × and ÷ by 10, 100, 1,000 and Ordering
standard_text: Understand and use place value for decimals, measures and integers of any size; order positive and negative integers, decimals and fractions; use the number line as a model for ordering of the real numbers; use the symbols =, ≠, <, >, ≤, ≥.
meta_desc: Free Year 7 maths worksheets on place value and ordering: the value of digits in decimals, multiplying and dividing by 10, 100 and 1,000, ordering decimals and negative numbers, and using < and >. 100 questions with answers.
key_big: Line up the decimal points and compare from the left: 0.6 is bigger than 0.508.
key_sub: On the number line, left is smaller: −7 < −3. Multiplying by 10 moves digits one place left.
body_html:
How it works

Each column is worth 10 times the column to its right. After the decimal point come tenths, hundredths and thousandths.

ThousandsHundredsTensOnes.TenthsHundredthsThousandths
4372.605

In 4,372.605 the 6 is worth 0.6 and the 5 is worth 0.005.

To compare decimals, line up the decimal points and compare from the left. On a number line, numbers get smaller as you go left, so −8 < −3.

Example

Order 0.6, 0.45, 0.508 and 0.09 from smallest to largest.

Write them with the same number of decimal places: 0.600, 0.450, 0.508, 0.090.

Compare: 0.090 < 0.450 < 0.508 < 0.600.

Answer: 0.09, 0.45, 0.508, 0.6

Example

Work out 3.47 × 100.

× 100 moves every digit 2 places to the left.

Answer: 347

Example

Which is smaller, −7 or −3?

−7 is further left on the number line.

Answer: −7

Common mistakes

  • Thinking 0.508 is bigger than 0.6 because it has more digits.
  • Moving the decimal point the wrong way: 34.7 ÷ 10 is 3.47, not 347.
  • Saying −7 is bigger than −3 because 7 is bigger than 3.
  • Giving the digit instead of its value: in 5.07 the 7 is worth 0.07, not 7.

−2 is bigger. It is closer to zero and further right on the number line.

faq.q: What happens when you multiply by 100?
faq.a: Every digit moves two places to the left, so 3.47 × 100 = 347.
It means “is less than”. The small end points to the smaller number: 3 < 8.
